To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the direct-form LMF adaptive filter has nearly same critical path as the transpose-form counterpart, (b) no pipelining or adaptation delays are required for implementing the direct-form LME adaptive filter for most cases, (c) a direct-form adaptive filter with only one adaptation delays can be used for high-speed implementation, and (d) the proposed direct-form LMS structures provide much better convergence, much lower register complexity and much lower EPS than the existing direct-form structures.
the direct-form structure has the same critical path and much faster convergence and less area than the transpose structure.
the direct-form structure of the LMS algorithm has a critical path similar to the transpose-form structure, and that pipelining is not necessary to implement a direct-form LMA adaptive filter.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design of the direct-form LMA adaptive filter, which has not been studied before.
the critical-path analysis and low-complex implementation of the LMS algorithm.
the design and analysis of direct-form LMS structures that are capable of high-speed implementation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Design 1 is suitable for most practical cases and is the most efficient structure of all the direct-form LMs adaptive filter structures.
the direct-form structure of the LMS algorithm is the best choice for most practical cases.
the LMS adaptive filtering algorithm is a very good candidate for high-speed implementation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
Design 1 is the best choice for applications with low-speed requirements, and Design 2 or Design 3 is recommended for applications with very high-speed requirements.
Design 1 is the most efficient structure for the LMS adaptive algorithm.
the direct-form structures of LMS adaptive filters are the best choice for high-speed and/or low-complexity implementations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a direct-form LTI adaptive filter is a viable choice for high-speed applications.
the LMS adaptive filters can be implemented with very high speed, very low complexity, and very small adaptation delays.
the LMS adaptive filters are very well suited for high-speed implementation.
